text:
alice-nguyen: Hey all, running into a weird one — redwoodctl local serve keeps picking my `personal` profile even when I pass `--profile work` and I explicitly set `REDWOOD_PROFILE=work` in the shell. Anyone seen this?
ben-cho: hm does `redwoodctl --version` match the latest? we had a recent profile lookup change.
alice-nguyen:  redwoodctl version 0.9.3 (installed via homebrew). Config file at ~/.redwood/config.json: 
```json
{"profiles": {"personal": {"token": "xxx"}, "work": {"token": "yyy"}}, "active_profile": "personal"}
```
I tried `redwoodctl config set active_profile work` and it reports success but local serve still uses the personal token (I see request logs showing personal account).
carla: can you paste the `redwoodctl local serve --debug` log? Also are you using zsh + a zsh plugin that might be exporting REDWOOD_PROFILE elsewhere? :eyes: 
alice-nguyen: debug output snippet: 
```
INFO reading config from /Users/alice/.config/redwood/config.json
INFO active_profile=personal
WARN env REDWOOD_PROFILE=work
INFO resolved_profile=personal
```
so it looks like it reads from XDG path `/Users/alice/.config/redwood/config.json` instead of `~/.redwood/config.json` even though both exist (old installer put file in home).
ben-cho: aha. installer historically wrote to ~/.redwood but newer code prefers XDG_CONFIG_HOME. If both exist we should respect explicit CLI `--profile` though.
alice-nguyen: yep that's the thing — `--profile work` is ignored. Repro steps: 1) create both config files with different active_profile, 2) run `REDWOOD_PROFILE=work redwoodctl local serve --profile work --debug` -> still resolves personal.
devx-bot: Created issue #4521 in devex/redwoodctl: "profile lookup priority ignores --profile arg when duplicate configs exist" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/4521 :white_check_mark:
sam-lee: I can reproduce on macOS 13 with homebrew 0.9.3. Looks like precedence code checks env then file in XDG path and then falls back to legacy path, but there's a logic bug where the CLI stops early after reading the first config file and doesn't apply explicit CLI arg override. I'll throw up a quick PR to short-circuit that.
tina-ortiz: temporary workaround for folks hitting this: `redwoodctl config set --path ~/.redwood/config.json active_profile work` or `mv ~/.config/redwood/config.json ~/.config/redwood/config.json.bak` then restart. Also you can `redwoodctl serve --token $(jq -r '.profiles.work.token' ~/.redwood/config.json)` to bypass profile resolution.
alice-nguyen: thanks Tina — `redwoodctl config set --path ~/.redwood/config.json active_profile work` worked for me. Confirmed local serve is using the work token now. :thumbsup:
sam-lee: PR opened: devex/redwoodctl#4530 branch fix/profile-lookup. Patch adds tests for precedence and ensures `--profile` and `REDWOOD_PROFILE` override any file choices. Assigning to eng-runtime for review.
infra-bot: Scheduled canary deploy for redwoodctl 0.9.4 in staging at 2026-03-24T02:00:00Z if PR merges.
ben-cho: quick follow-up — we should add an integration test in CI that creates both XDG and legacy config and validates CLI arg precedence. Filing follow-up task.
carla: nice catch, Sam. tagging eng-platform to update the installer docs to mention XDG vs legacy paths to avoid confusion.
alice-nguyen: grateful for the quick turnaround. Will unsubscribe from the thread after this is fixed.
devx-bot: Closing note: if you hit other profile oddities, react with :eyes: and include `redwoodctl --debug` output so we can triage quickly.
